([[Wilmington, Delaware]]) | nationality = American | college = [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] (2015–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 17 | draft_team = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | career_start = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2018|start}}–{{nbay|2021|end}} | team1 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years2 = 2018 | team2 = →[[Wisconsin Herd]] | years3 = {{nbay|2021|end}} | team3 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years4 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team4 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team5 = [[New York Knicks]] | years6 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team6 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]) * 2× [[List of NCAA Division I Men's Basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2016]], [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018]]) * [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] ([[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018]]) * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]] (2018) * Big East All-Freshman team (2017) }} '''Donte Michael DiVincenzo''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|ɒ|n|t|eɪ|_|ˌ|d|iː|v|ɪ|n|ˈ|tʃ|ɛ|n|z|oʊ}} {{respell|DON|tay|_|DEE|vin|CHEN|zoh}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born January 31, 1997) is an Italian-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]], where he won national championships in [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2016]] and [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018]], being named [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP) in 2018. Selected with the 17th overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], DiVincenzo won his first championship with the Bucks in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]], before being traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] the following season. He has since played for the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[New York Knicks]], and Minnesota Timberwolves. He holds the Knicks franchise records for single-game and single-season three-point shots made. ==Early life== DiVincenzo was born in [[Newark, Delaware]], to parents John F. and Kathie DiVincenzo. He has a brother, John, and a sister, Allison.{{Cite web |title=Donte DiVincenzo - Men's Basketball |url=https://villanova.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/donte-divincenzo/396 |access-date=2023-12-31 |website=Villanova University |language=en}} Growing up, he played [[soccer]] before switching to basketball in high school.{{cite news|last1=Schonbrun|first1=Zach|title=Donte DiVincenzo and Trevon Duval Give Delaware Hoops a Moment|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/23/sports/delaware-march-madness.html|access-date=March 31, 2018|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 23, 2018|archive-date=June 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613015402/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/23/sports/delaware-march-madness.html|url-status=live}} DiVincenzo attended [[Salesianum School]] in Wilmington, Delaware, where he led the team to back-to-back state championships. As a junior, he averaged 15.8 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game and played basketball in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] for Team Final. He averaged 22.9 points, 9.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game as a senior. He was named Delaware Sportswriters and Broadcasters Association's Boys' Basketball Player of the Year in 2015.{{cite web|title=10 Donte DiVincenzo|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/donte_divincenzo_979537.html|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|access-date=March 31, 2018|archive-date=June 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613014725/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/donte_divincenzo_979537.html|url-status=dead}} In 2025, he gained Italian citizenship.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/uk/nba/milwaukee-bucks/news/former-bucks-champion-receives-italian-citizenship/e35a7dd48abb1c4f0ab2c436|title=Former Bucks champion receives Italian citizenship | Sporting News|date=July 15, 2025|website=www.sportingnews.com}} ==College career== [[File:20170213 Villanova-Depaul Donte DiVincenzo watches free throw.jpg|thumb|left|DiVincenzo with [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] in 2017]] DiVincenzo appeared in nine games during his true freshman year{{cite web|title=Donte DiVincenzo|publisher=Sports Reference – College Basketball|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/donte-divincenzo-1.html|access-date=June 25, 2018|archive-date=June 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180626030213/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/donte-divincenzo-1.html|url-status=live}} for Villanova before sitting out with a fractured fifth metatarsal bone in his right foot. The following season, in his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] freshman season, DiVincenzo averaged 8.8 points and 3.8 rebounds per game. He registered 19 points, three rebounds, and two assists in a 70–57 victory against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] on January 14, 2017. On March 9, DiVincenzo had a season-high 25 points to go with five rebounds and four assists in a 108–67 rematch win over St. John's. In the NCAA Tournament, he scored 21 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a 76–56 victory over [[Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball|Mount St. Mary's]] in the first round. DiVincenzo was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman team and the [[Philadelphia Big 5|Philadelphia Big Five]] Rookie of the Year. In his sophomore season, DiVincenzo had a then career-high 30 points in an 86–75 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] on February 10, 2018.{{cite news|title=Donte DiVincenzo, Jalen Brunson lead Villanova past Butler|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988606|access-date=March 31, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 10, 2018|archive-date=April 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180401004528/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400988606|url-status=live}} At the conclusion of the regular season, he was named Big East [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Sixth Man of the Year|Sixth Man of the Year]].{{cite news|last1=Juliano|first1=Joe|title=Villanova's Donte DiVincenzo wins Big East Sixth Man award|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/villanova-big-east-basketball-donte-divincenzo-ncaa-tournament-20180305.html|access-date=March 31, 2018|work=[[The DiVincenzo was named the NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player following their championship win over Michigan, in which he scored a career-high 31 points (including five three-point baskets) and recorded five rebounds, three assists and two blocked shots. In addition, he scored the most points in an NCAA Final Four game for a player coming off the bench.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=2018-04-03 |title=Beilein: We had no answer for MOP DiVincenzo |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23007836/villanova-donte-divincenzo-wins-most-outstanding-player-final-four |access-date=2025-07-12 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} DiVincenzo was dubbed the "Big [[Ragù|Ragu]]" by sportscaster [[Gus Johnson (sportscaster)|Gus Johnson]] following his last-second [[Tip-in (basketball)|tip-in]] in a game on January 29, 2017, which gave Villanova the win against the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|University of Virginia]]. The nickname was given to him ostensibly due to his Italian heritage and his red hair. When Johnson came up with the nickname, he was probably referring to another "Big Ragu", a character named [[Carmine Ragusa]] on the 1970s–80s sitcom ''[[Laverne & Shirley]]'', who was also Italian.{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/who-is-donte-divincenzo-all-you-need-to-know-about-villanovas-big-ragu/ |title=Who is Donte DiVincenzo? All you need to know about Villanova's 'Big Ragu' |last=Kercheval |first=Ben |work=CBSSports.com |access-date=April 3, 2018 |language=en |archive-date=April 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403101402/https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/who-is-donte-divincenzo-all-you-need-to-know-about-villanovas-big-ragu/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/04/02/villanova-donte-divincenzo-fast-facts|title=What you need to Know about Villanova's Donte DiVincenzo|work=SI.com|access-date=April 3, 2018|language=en|archive-date=April 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404073058/https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/04/02/villanova-donte-divincenzo-fast-facts|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/04/donte-divincenzo-big-ragu|title=This is how Donte DiVincenzo got the nickname 'The Big Ragu'|work=USA Today|access-date=April 9, 2018|language=en|archive-date=April 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409171800/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2018/04/donte-divincenzo-big-ragu|url-status=live}} On April 19, 2018, DiVincenzo announced he would declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without hiring an agent, thereby leaving open the possibility of a return to Villanova. On May 29, 2018, DiVincenzo announced he would remain in the draft and hire an agent, forgoing his final two years of eligibility at Villanova.{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/05/29/donte-divincenzo-stays-2018-nba-draft-foregoes-ncaa-eligibility |title=DiVincenzo stays in 2018 NBA draft, foregoes NCAA eligibility |website=SI.com |language=en |access-date=2019-05-24 |archive-date=May 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190524182034/https://www.si.com/nba/2018/05/29/donte-divincenzo-stays-2018-nba-draft-foregoes-ncaa-eligibility |url-status=live }} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2018–2022)=== On June 21, 2018, DiVincenzo was selected with the 17th overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], the second of four Villanova players drafted that year.{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/Bucks/status/1009969746455007233|title=Milwaukee Bucks on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=June 22, 2018|language=en}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-select-donte-divincenzo-17th-pick-2018-nba-draft|title=Milwaukee Bucks Select Donte DiVincenzo with 17th Pick in 2018 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 22, 2018|archive-date=June 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622193812/https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-select-donte-divincenzo-17th-pick-2018-nba-draft|url-status=live}} On July 10, 2018, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that they had signed DiVincenzo.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-sign-donte-divincenzo|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Donte DiVincenzo|date=July 10, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 10, 2018|archive-date=July 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180728000906/https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-sign-donte-divincenzo|url-status=live}} He missed most of his rookie season with a foot injury. He shot a career-high 39.7% from three-point range on 5.3 attempts per game.{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=2023-07-02 |title=Knicks to add DiVincenzo on 4-year, $50M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37946638/knicks-add-donte-divincenzo-four-year-50m-deal |access-date=2023-12-31 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} In June 2023, DiVincenzo turned down a $4.7 million player option for the second season and opted for free agency. ===New York Knicks (2023–2024)=== [[File:Knicks vs Nets (DiVincenzo 1).jpg|thumb|DiVincenzo with the Knicks]] On July 8, 2023, DiVincenzo signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Donte DiVincenzo|number=1677837888195788800|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} He agreed to a four-year, $50 million deal with the Knicks. He joined Villanova teammates [[Jalen Brunson]] and [[Josh Hart]]. On March 25, 2024, DiVincenzo scored a career-high 40 points in a 124–99 victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. During this game, he also scored 11 three-pointers, setting a new Knicks franchise record for three-pointers in a single game.{{Cite web |last=Blinn |first=Michael |date=2024-03-26 |title=Donte DiVincenzo sets Knicks' single-game 3-point record |url=https://nypost.com/2024/03/25/sports/donte-divincenzo-sets-knicks-single-game-3-point-record/ |access-date=2024-03-26 |language=en-US|work=[[New York Post]]}} He finished the season with a franchise single-season record 283 three point shots made.{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2024/04/17/sports/knicks-donte-divincenzo-ineligible-for-nba-awards/|title=Knicks’ Donte DiVincenzo ineligible for NBA awards due to league caveats|accessdate=April 18, 2024|date=April 17, 2024|work=[[New York Post]]|author=Arnold, Christian}} On April 22, 2024, DiVincenzo put up 19 points, including the game-winning three-pointer, in the Knicks' 104–101 victory in game 2 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-vs-knicks-game-2-breakdown|title=76ers vs. Knicks Game 2 breakdown: NY steals win in unreal late sequence|website=ClutchPoints|last=DiGiovanni|first=Sam|date=April 22, 2024|access-date=April 22, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/knicks-news-donte-divincenzos-reaction-unreal-win-76ers-give-fans-goosebumps|title=Knicks sharpshooter Donte DiVincenzo's reaction to unreal win vs 76ers will give fans goosebumps|website=ClutchPoints|last=Valdez|first=Joshua|date=April 22, 2024|access-date=April 22, 2024}} In the second round against the [[Indiana Pacers]], DiVincenzo set an NBA record for most three point shots made in a playoff game 7 (9).{{cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2024/05/19/knicks-donte-divincenzo-most-three-pointers-game-7-history/|title=Knicks’ Donte DiVincenzo’s 9 made threes most ever in Game 7 history|accessdate=May 22, 2024|date=May 19, 2024|work=[[New York Daily News]]|author=Frimpong, Fiifi}} His 6 in the second half also set a game 7 record for threes in a half. Both records were tied by [[Buddy Hield]] on May 4, 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/buddy-hield-shuts-up-hater-warriors-fans-record-20309805.php|title=Buddy Hield shuts up hater Warriors fans with record-breaking Game 7|accessdate=May 6, 2025|date=May 4, 2025|publisher=[[SFGate]]|author=Fernandez, Gabe}} Ironically, Divincenzo's role on the [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team]] that won the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national title]] was to impersonate Hield for the scout team.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/ncaa-basketball/villanova-basketball-news-donte-divincenzo-buddy-hield-impersonation-title|title=How Donte DiVincenzo’s Buddy Hield scout helped win a national title at Villanova|accessdate=May 6, 2025|date=October 14, 2024|website=[[ClutchPoints]]|author=Finnegan, Tom}} The Knicks were eliminated in seven games despite a 39-point performance from DiVincenzo in a 130–109 game 7 loss.{{Cite web|last=Selbe|first=Nick|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers-beat-knicks-game-7-eastern-conference-finals|title=Pacers Beat Knicks in Game 7, Advance to Eastern Conference Finals|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 19, 2024|access-date=May 20, 2024}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2024–present)=== On October 2, 2024, DiVincenzo, [[Keita Bates-Diop]], [[Julius Randle]], and one lottery protected first–round pick were traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves as part of a three-team trade with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in which Charlotte received, via sign-and-trade, [[DaQuan Jeffries]], [[Charlie Brown Jr. (basketball)|Charlie Brown Jr.]], [[Duane Washington Jr.]], three second-round picks and financial compensation. The Knicks acquired [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and the draft rights to [[James Nnaji]].{{cite web|first=Taylor|last=Nardinger|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Forward Keita Bates-Diop, Guard Donte DiVincenzo and Forward Julius Randle from New York Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-forward-keita-bates-diop-guard-donte-divincenzo-and-forward-julius-randle-from-new-york-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 2, 2024}} DiVincenzo started all 82 games for the Timberwolves during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 12.2 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} In Game 4 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs|2026 first round]], Divincenzo [[Achilles tendon rupture|tore his Achilles]] after an awkward landing in the first quarter, ruling him out for the remainder of the playoffs and likely the
